claims: The Artemis II mission concluded on April 10, 2026.
The Artemis II mission concluded with a splashdown in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California.
The Orion capsule landed around 5:07 p.m. PDT (8:07 p.m. EDT).
The Orion capsule landed approximately 40 to 50 miles offshore.
The Artemis II mission was a 10-day crewed mission around the Moon.
US Navy vessels and specialized teams were positioned for retrieval near San Diego, as noted in the CNN live report and cbs8.com.
The reentry caused a sonic boom.
The landing was too far offshore for clear public viewing.
The crew and capsule were transported back to Naval Air Station North Island in Coronado, California, for post-landing evaluations.
